title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (single-phase BCC solid solution).
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of the quaternary alloy with a few atomic-percent rhenium, followed by heavy-ion (e.g., 3–5 MeV Fe or Kr) irradiation at elevated temperature to compare the Re-containing alloy with the Re-free baseline.
recollection.structure: Remains a BCC solid solution but with short-range chemical ordering; irradiation produces far fewer dislocation loops and voids in the Re-doped alloy than in the undoped alloy.
recollection.mechanism: Re introduces local chemical/size misfit that increases point-defect trapping and promotes recombination of vacancies and interstitials, thereby suppressing cascade growth and loop formation. It also stabilises chemical short-range order that impedes defect migration.
recollection.results: Compared with NbMoTaW, the NbMoTaWRe alloy shows ~30–50 % lower irradiation-induced hardening, >2× reduction in dislocation-loop density, and negligible (<0.1 %) volumetric swelling up to ~10 dpa at 800 °C. (Values are approximate; guess.)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies Re addition and comparison with irradiated NbMoTaW, but incorrectly describes dilute Re substitution and MeV Fe/Kr irradiation rather than equiatomic NbMoTaWRe implanted with 120 keV He2+. The single-BCC description and reduced irradiation damage are broadly consistent, while the claimed short-range order, dislocation loops, and voids are unsupported; the actual key features were grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and suppression of grain-boundary He bubbles. The proposed defect trapping/recombination mechanism substantially overlaps the reported defect-sink mechanism, although its emphasis on short-range order and loop suppression is incorrect. All numerical hardening, loop-density, swelling, dose, and temperature claims are guessed and inconsistent with the reported measurements.
